questions.q: Cyclohexene is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ to give an intermediate organic product 'A'. Product 'A' is then heated strongly with excess ammonia to give the final product 'B'. The IUPAC name of product 'B' is:
questions.question: Cyclohexene is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ to give an intermediate organic product 'A'. Product 'A' is then heated strongly with excess ammonia to give the final product 'B'. The IUPAC name of product 'B' is:
questions.solution:
Cyclohexene undergoes oxidative cleavage of the double bond upon treatment with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, opening the ring to form hexanedioic acid (adipic acid) as product 'A'.

When hexanedioic acid is heated strongly with excess ammonia, it first forms an ammonium salt which on strong heating loses water molecules to form an amide. Since it is a dicarboxylic acid, both carboxyl groups are converted to amide groups, yielding hexanediamide (adipamide) as product 'B'.

Reaction:
Cyclohexene $\rightarrow$ $\text{HOOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{COOH}$ (Product A)
$\text{HOOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{COOH}$ + excess $\text{NH}_3$ + strong heat $\rightarrow$ $\text{H}_2\text{NOC}-(\text{CH}_2)_4-\text{CONH}_2$ (Product B)

Answer: Hexanediamide

(B) $p$-Chlorotoluene + $\text{KMnO}_4/\text{H}^+$(II) Product is a weaker acid than benzoic acid
(C) $p$-Nitroanisole + $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$(III) Product is a stronger base than aniline
(D) $p$-Chloronitrobenzene + $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$(IV) Product is a weaker base than aniline

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
(A) Oxidation of $p$-methoxytoluene with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields $p$-methoxybenzoic acid. The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group has a strong $+M$ effect which outweighs its $-I$ effect, making the product a weaker acid than benzoic acid. (Matches II)

(B) Oxidation of $p$-chlorotoluene yields $p$-chlorobenzoic acid. For halogens, the $-I$ effect outweighs the $+M$ effect, making the product a stronger acid than benzoic acid. (Matches I)

(C) Reduction of $p$-nitroanisole with $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$ yields $p$-anisidine. The $+M$ effect of the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group increases electron density on the nitrogen, making the product a stronger base than aniline. (Matches III)

(D) Reduction of $p$-chloronitrobenzene yields $p$-chloroaniline. The net electron-withdrawing nature of chlorine ($-I > +M$) decreases electron density on the nitrogen, making the product a weaker base than aniline. (Matches IV)

The correct matching is (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV).

Answer: (A)-(II), (B)-(I), (C)-(III), (D)-(IV)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown alkene 'X' with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_8H_{16}}$ undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield two moles of a single compound 'Y'. Compound 'Y' gives a positive Iodoform test but fails to give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. Identify the IUPAC name of alkene 'X'.
questions.question: An unknown alkene 'X' with molecular formula $\mathrm{C_8H_{16}}$ undergoes reductive ozonolysis to yield two moles of a single compound 'Y'. Compound 'Y' gives a positive Iodoform test but fails to give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent. Identify the IUPAC name of alkene 'X'.
questions.solution:
Since alkene 'X' gives two moles of a single compound 'Y' on reductive ozonolysis, 'X' must be a symmetrical alkene.

Compound 'Y' does not give a silver mirror with Tollens' reagent, indicating it is a ketone, not an aldehyde. It gives a positive Iodoform test, which means it is a methyl ketone (contains a $\mathrm{-COCH_3}$ group).

Given the molecular formula of 'X' is $\mathrm{C_8H_{16}}$, compound 'Y' must have 4 carbon atoms ($\mathrm{C_4H_8O}$). The only 4-carbon methyl ketone is butan-2-one ($\mathrm{CH_3COCH_2CH_3}$).

Connecting two molecules of butan-2-one at their carbonyl carbons gives the structure of alkene 'X': $\mathrm{CH_3CH_2C(CH_3)=C(CH_3)CH_2CH_3}$, which is 3,4-dimethylhex-3-ene.

Oct-4-ene and 2,5-dimethylhex-3-ene would yield aldehydes (butanal and 2-methylpropanal respectively), which are Tollens positive. 2,4,4-Trimethylpent-2-ene would yield a mixture of two different compounds.

Answer: 3,4-Dimethylhex-3-ene

questions.q:
Match the alkenes in List-I with their respective major products obtained upon vigorous oxidation with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ in List-II.

List-I (Alkene)List-II (Oxidation Products)
A. 2-Methylbut-2-eneI. Butanedioic acid
B. Pent-2-eneII. Ethanoic acid and Propanoic acid
C. 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-eneIII. Propanone and Ethanoic acid
D. CyclobuteneIV. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid and $\text{CO}_2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Match the alkenes in List-I with their respective major products obtained upon vigorous oxidation with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ in List-II.

List-I (Alkene)List-II (Oxidation Products)
A. 2-Methylbut-2-eneI. Butanedioic acid
B. Pent-2-eneII. Ethanoic acid and Propanoic acid
C. 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-eneIII. Propanone and Ethanoic acid
D. CyclobuteneIV. 2,2-Dimethylpropanoic acid and $\text{CO}_2$

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution:
Vigorous oxidation of alkenes with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ leads to the cleavage of the $\text{C}=\text{C}$ double bond.

A. 2-Methylbut-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{C}(\text{CH}_3)=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$) has one vinylic carbon with no hydrogen and one with a hydrogen. It cleaves to form a ketone (propanone) and a carboxylic acid (ethanoic acid). (A $\rightarrow$ III)

B. Pent-2-ene ($\text{CH}_3-\text{CH}_2-\text{CH}=\text{CH}-\text{CH}_3$) is an internal alkene with hydrogens on both vinylic carbons. It cleaves to form propanoic acid and ethanoic acid. (B $\rightarrow$ II)

C. 3,3-Dimethylbut-1-ene ($(\text{CH}_3)_3\text{C}-\text{CH}=\text{CH}_2$) is a terminal alkene. The terminal $=\text{CH}_2$ group is oxidized to $\text{CO}_2$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, while the other part becomes 2,2-dimethylpropanoic acid. (C $\rightarrow$ IV)

D. Cyclobutene is a cyclic alkene. Oxidative cleavage opens the four-membered ring to form a dicarboxylic acid with four carbons, which is butanedioic acid (succinic acid). (D $\rightarrow$ I)

Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I.

Answer: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: A secondary alcohol 'P' on oxidation with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ gives compound 'Q'. Compound 'Q' can also be synthesized by the reaction of benzene with propanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$. Identify the alcohol 'P'.
questions.question: A secondary alcohol 'P' on oxidation with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ gives compound 'Q'. Compound 'Q' can also be synthesized by the reaction of benzene with propanoyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$. Identify the alcohol 'P'.
questions.solution:
The reaction of benzene with propanoyl chloride ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts acylation. It yields propiophenone (1-phenylpropan-1-one) as compound 'Q'.

Compound 'Q' is also formed by the oxidation of a secondary alcohol 'P' with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$. Therefore, 'P' must be the secondary alcohol corresponding to propiophenone.

Reducing the ketone group of 1-phenylpropan-1-one gives 1-phenylpropan-1-ol. Thus, 'P' is 1-phenylpropan-1-ol.

1-Phenylpropan-2-ol would oxidize to 1-phenylpropan-2-one. 3-Phenylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, and 2-phenylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol which resists oxidation.

Answer: 1-Phenylpropan-1-ol
questions.explanation:
The reaction of benzene with propanoyl chloride ($\mathrm{CH_3CH_2COCl}$) in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ is a Friedel-Crafts acylation. It yields propiophenone (1-phenylpropan-1-one) as compound 'Q'.

Compound 'Q' is also formed by the oxidation of a secondary alcohol 'P' with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$. Therefore, 'P' must be the secondary alcohol corresponding to propiophenone.

Reducing the ketone group of 1-phenylpropan-1-one gives 1-phenylpropan-1-ol. Thus, 'P' is 1-phenylpropan-1-ol.

1-Phenylpropan-2-ol would oxidize to 1-phenylpropan-2-one. 3-Phenylpropan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, and 2-phenylpropan-2-ol is a tertiary alcohol which resists oxidation.

Answer: 1-Phenylpropan-1-ol

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding the oxidation or reduction products of substituted aromatic compounds is incorrect?
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the oxidation or reduction products of substituted aromatic compounds is incorrect?
options: Oxidation of $p$-nitrotoluene with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid stronger than $p$-fluorobenzoic acid.
Reduction of $p$-nitroanisole with Sn/HCl gives an amine that is a stronger base than aniline.
Reduction of $m$-chloronitrobenzene with Sn/HCl gives an amine that is a weaker base than aniline.
Oxidation of $m$-methoxytoluene with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid weaker than benzoic acid due to the $+M$ effect of the methoxy group.
questions.solution:
Let us evaluate each statement.

Statement 1 is correct: Oxidation of $p$-nitrotoluene yields $p$-nitrobenzoic acid. The $-\text{NO}_2$ group is a strong electron-withdrawing group ($-I, -M$), making it a stronger acid than $p$-fluorobenzoic acid, where fluorine has a weaker net electron-withdrawing effect.

Statement 2 is correct: Reduction of $p$-nitroanisole yields $p$-anisidine. The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group is an electron-donating group ($+M > -I$), which increases electron density on the nitrogen, making it a stronger base than aniline.

Statement 3 is correct: Reduction of $m$-chloronitrobenzene yields $m$-chloroaniline. The chlorine atom exerts a $-I$ effect, withdrawing electron density and making it a weaker base than aniline.

Statement 4 is incorrect: Oxidation of $m$-methoxytoluene yields $m$-methoxybenzoic acid. At the meta position, the mesomeric ($+M$) effect of the $-\text{OCH}_3$ group does not operate. Only its inductive ($-I$) effect is felt at the carboxyl group. Because of this $-I$ effect, $m$-methoxybenzoic acid is actually a stronger acid than benzoic acid, not weaker.

Answer: Oxidation of $m$-methoxytoluene with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid weaker than benzoic acid due to the $+M$ effect of the methoxy group.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
How many of the following reactions will yield a ketone as one of the major organic products?

(i) Ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene followed by reaction with $\mathrm{Zn/H_2O}$
(ii) Reaction of benzene with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$
(iii) Oxidation of butan-2-ol with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$
(iv) Oxidation of toluene with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ followed by heating
(v) Ozonolysis of propene followed by reaction with $\mathrm{Zn/H_2O}$
questions.question:
How many of the following reactions will yield a ketone as one of the major organic products?

(i) Ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene followed by reaction with $\mathrm{Zn/H_2O}$
(ii) Reaction of benzene with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$
(iii) Oxidation of butan-2-ol with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$
(iv) Oxidation of toluene with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ followed by heating
(v) Ozonolysis of propene followed by reaction with $\mathrm{Zn/H_2O}$
questions.solution:
(i) Ozonolysis of 2,3-dimethylbut-2-ene followed by $\mathrm{Zn/H_2O}$ (reductive ozonolysis) yields two molecules of propanone (acetone), which is a ketone.

(ii) Benzene reacts with acetyl chloride in the presence of anhydrous $\mathrm{AlCl_3}$ (Friedel-Crafts acylation) to yield acetophenone, which is a ketone.

(iii) Oxidation of butan-2-ol (a secondary alcohol) with $\mathrm{CrO_3}$ yields butan-2-one, which is a ketone.

(iv) Oxidation of toluene with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$ and heat yields potassium benzoate, which is a salt of a carboxylic acid, not a ketone.

(v) Reductive ozonolysis of propene yields ethanal (acetaldehyde) and methanal (formaldehyde), both of which are aldehydes, not ketones.

Therefore, exactly 3 reactions yield a ketone as a major product.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: What is the major organic product formed when 1-methylcyclopentene is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$?
questions.question: What is the major organic product formed when 1-methylcyclopentene is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$?
questions.solution:
When 1-methylcyclopentene is treated with hot acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$, the internal $\text{C=C}$ double bond undergoes complete oxidative cleavage, resulting in the opening of the five-membered ring.

The doubly bonded carbon atom bearing the methyl group has no vinylic hydrogen atoms, so it is oxidized to a ketone group.

The other doubly bonded carbon atom has one vinylic hydrogen atom, so it is oxidized to a carboxylic acid group.

The resulting straight-chain molecule contains six carbon atoms in total: the five carbons from the ring and the one from the methyl group.

Numbering from the carboxylic acid carbon as position 1, the ketone carbonyl is at position 5.

Therefore, the structure of the product is $\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-COOH}$, and its IUPAC name is 5-oxohexanoic acid.

Answer: 5-Oxohexanoic acid

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q:
Compound X is an isomer of nitrotoluene. Oxidation of X with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives the strongest acid among its isomers. Reduction of X with $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$ gives the weakest base among its isomers.

Identify Compound X.
questions.question:
Compound X is an isomer of nitrotoluene. Oxidation of X with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ gives the strongest acid among its isomers. Reduction of X with $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$ gives the weakest base among its isomers.

Identify Compound X.
questions.solution:
Isomers of nitrotoluene are $o$-nitrotoluene, $m$-nitrotoluene, and $p$-nitrotoluene.

Oxidation of these isomers with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields $o$-nitrobenzoic acid, $m$-nitrobenzoic acid, and $p$-nitrobenzoic acid, respectively. Due to the ortho-effect (a combination of steric and electronic factors), ortho-substituted benzoic acids are generally stronger acids than their meta and para isomers. Thus, $o$-nitrobenzoic acid is the strongest acid among them.

Reduction of the isomers with $\text{Sn}/\text{HCl}$ yields $o$-toluidine, $m$-toluidine, and $p$-toluidine, respectively. Due to the ortho-effect (steric inhibition of solvation of the conjugate acid), ortho-substituted anilines are weaker bases than their meta and para isomers, as well as aniline itself. Thus, $o$-toluidine is the weakest base among them.

Therefore, Compound X must be $o$-nitrotoluene.

Answer: $o$-Nitrotoluene

questions.q:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tert-Butylbenzene undergoes oxidation to benzoic acid when heated with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$.

Reason (R): The oxidation of an alkylbenzene to benzoic acid requires the presence of at least one benzylic hydrogen atom on the alkyl chain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.question:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): tert-Butylbenzene undergoes oxidation to benzoic acid when heated with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$.

Reason (R): The oxidation of an alkylbenzene to benzoic acid requires the presence of at least one benzylic hydrogen atom on the alkyl chain.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.solution:
Assertion (A) is false. tert-Butylbenzene does not undergo oxidation to benzoic acid when heated with alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$.

Reason (R) is true. For an alkylbenzene to be oxidized to benzoic acid by strong oxidizing agents like alkaline $\mathrm{KMnO_4}$, the alkyl group must have at least one benzylic hydrogen atom. In tert-butylbenzene, the benzylic carbon is attached to three methyl groups and has no benzylic hydrogen atoms. Therefore, it resists oxidation.

Hence, (A) is false but (R) is true.

Answer: (A) is false but (R) is true

questions.q:
Compound P on oxidation with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid that is less acidic than benzoic acid.
Compound Q on reduction with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is less basic than aniline.

Identify P and Q from the given options:
questions.question:
Compound P on oxidation with acidic KMnO$_4$ gives an acid that is less acidic than benzoic acid.
Compound Q on reduction with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is less basic than aniline.

Identify P and Q from the given options:
questions.solution:
For compound P to yield an acid less acidic than benzoic acid upon oxidation, the resulting benzoic acid derivative must contain an electron-donating group (EDG) that destabilizes the carboxylate conjugate base. The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group in $p$-methoxytoluene exerts a $+M$ effect, making $p$-methoxybenzoic acid a weaker acid than benzoic acid. If P were $p$-nitrotoluene, it would yield $p$-nitrobenzoic acid, which is stronger due to the $-M$ effect of $-\text{NO}_2$.

For compound Q to yield an amine less basic than aniline upon reduction, the resulting aniline derivative must contain an electron-withdrawing group (EWG) that decreases electron density on the nitrogen atom. The $-\text{Cl}$ group in $p$-chloronitrobenzene reduces to $p$-chloroaniline, where the $-I$ effect of chlorine makes it a weaker base than aniline. If Q were $p$-nitroanisole or $p$-methylnitrobenzene, they would reduce to $p$-anisidine and $p$-toluidine respectively, both of which are stronger bases than aniline due to the $+M$ and $+I$/hyperconjugation effects of their substituents.

Therefore, P is $p$-methoxytoluene and Q is $p$-chloronitrobenzene.

Answer: P = $p$-Methoxytoluene, Q = $p$-Chloronitrobenzene

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: An unknown alkene 'X' on vigorous oxidation with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields a mixture of propan-2-one and ethanoic acid as the major organic products. The IUPAC name of the alkene 'X' is:
questions.question: An unknown alkene 'X' on vigorous oxidation with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ yields a mixture of propan-2-one and ethanoic acid as the major organic products. The IUPAC name of the alkene 'X' is:
questions.solution:
Vigorous oxidation of alkenes with acidic $\text{KMnO}_4$ cleaves the $\text{C=C}$ double bond.

The products are propan-2-one ($\text{CH}_3\text{-CO-CH}_3$) and ethanoic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$).

Propan-2-one is a ketone, which indicates that one of the doubly bonded carbons was disubstituted, specifically a $\text{=C(CH}_3)_2$ group.

Ethanoic acid is a carboxylic acid, which indicates that the other doubly bonded carbon had one hydrogen atom and one methyl group, specifically a $\text{=CH-CH}_3$ group.

Joining these two fragments at the double bond gives the structure of the original alkene 'X': $\text{(CH}_3)_2\text{C=CH-CH}_3$.

The IUPAC name of this compound is 2-methylbut-2-ene.

Answer: 2-Methylbut-2-ene
